Samir — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front, details below.

- Fallback/overage: our standard behavior for private offers is to apply committed credits first; any usage above the committed monthly allowance is billed as overage at the contracted overage rate (which is typically a step-up from the hosted list price but lower than on-demand). We do not silently throttle requests; we prefer explicit overage billing to avoid API errors for customer production traffic.

- Invoice phasing/proration: committed credits are delivered as monthly credit rows on the GCP invoice tied to the private offer. If credits are front-loaded in the first month, we include a proration line that splits the credit across the remaining months in the contract term as requested — that can be done but must be agreed in the term sheet (it changes how we schedule redemption in the marketplace entitlement).

SKU mapping: the committed units map to the marketplace entitlement line: redwood:inference.v1.compute (we'll provide the exact SKU id in the next email). Overage shows as a distinct line item on the same monthly invoice.

Actions I propose:
- Marissa / Karthik: can you confirm the exact SKU id and the precise overage unit price for the DH private offer?
- Samir: can you confirm the target monthly burn you expect for Q3 so we can produce a worked example invoice and the proration schedule? Your attached forecast helps but we need a one-line monthly target to example-run.

If helpful, we can also provide a fallback option that allows automatic temporary spill to Redwood-hosted with throttling if the customer explicitly prefers availability-first behavior; that would need a different billing construct (hosted overage billed on top of credits) and an explicit service-level note in the term sheet.

I'll draft a short note with SKU and two invoice examples (1: standard monthly credits + overage; 2: front-loaded credits with proration) once I have Karthik's SKU numbers and your one-line target.

Thanks — R
